item.text:
**7B.4 Research Note**

Overall read: **mostly no**. I found strong evidence of regime-security capture, opaque foundations, and insider control over revenue and candidate access. I did **not** find a clean 2024 document showing a named Khamenei family payout, bribe, or contract windfall, so the case is structural rather than a single smoking gun.

| Claim-level item | Publisher | Date | URL | Short claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| [Iran’s Revolutionary Guards extend control over Tehran’s oil exports, sources say](https://www.investing.com/news/commodities-news/irans-revolutionary-guards-extend-control-over-tehrans-oil-exports-sources-say-3778558) | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-12-18 | https://www.investing.com/news/commodities-news/irans-revolutionary-guards-extend-control-over-tehrans-oil-exports-sources-say-3778558 | Strong negative evidence: Reuters reported the IRGC controlled up to half of Iran’s oil exports, using shadow fleets and front companies. Since oil revenue funds state spending, this looks like capture of a core state asset by regime-security networks, not separation from office. | 7B.4, 7B.3, 6B.10 |
| [Iran: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report](https://freedomhouse.org/country/iran/freedom-world/2024) | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/iran/freedom-world/2024 | Strong structural negative: Freedom House says corruption is endemic and IRGC/bonyads are above scrutiny, with broad economic power and weak accountability. That is direct evidence of opaque conflicts of interest and privileged access. | 7B.4, 7B.3, 6B.10, 7B.1 |
| [Iran's presidential election dominated by Khamenei loyalists](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/irans-presidential-election-dominated-by-khamenei-loyalists-3494879) | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-06-25 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/irans-presidential-election-dominated-by-khamenei-loyalists-3494879 | Strong negative evidence: Reuters said Khamenei ensured hardline candidates dominated the contest, the Guardian Council approved only five hardliners and one low-profile moderate from 80 applicants, and Khamenei controlled the bulk of financial resources. That is insider filtering and resource control, not clean separation. | 7B.4, 7B.3, 7B.1 |

That means oversight is not independent enough to police hidden conflicts or family-linked enrichment. | 7B.4, 6B.9, 7B.3 |

This suggests some competence-based staffing existed, but it looks compromise-driven and does not show clean separation from patronage politics. | 7B.4, 7B.3, 6B.10 |

**Search gap**

I did not find a 2024 source naming a direct Khamenei family enrichment event, specific bribe, or family-held contract. The evidence I found is broader and more structural: control over oil exports, opaque foundations, security-network revenue, and loyalty-based access.

**Bottom line**

Best-supported judgment: **yes, in practice the office is entangled with opaque, privilege-bearing networks; no clean separation is evident**. The strongest evidence points to captured revenue streams and institutionally protected insider access, while the best counter-signal is only limited technocratic staffing.
